title: Tenali Raman and the Disputed Elephant Calf
summary: Two timber merchants from the Malabar border, Keshav and Madhav, appeared before King Krishnadevaraya's court, dragging a playful young elephant calf on a rope. Both men claimed...
full_text:
Two timber merchants from the Malabar border, Keshav and Madhav, appeared before King Krishnadevaraya's court, dragging a playful young elephant calf on a rope. Both men claimed ownership of the calf.
Keshav swore: 'The calf was born to my working cow-elephant, Lakshmi, six months ago! Madhav stole it from my forest corral!'
Madhav shouted: 'Liar! It was born to my cow-elephant, Gauri, in the river valley! I have three witnesses who saw the birth!'

Because both merchants presented stamped sales certificates and sworn witnesses, the royal judges were completely divided.
The King turned to Tenali Raman:
'Tenali, settle this dispute, for the judges cannot read the minds of elephants.'

Tenali smiled: 'Maharaj, the court of humans may be confused by forged seals, but the court of nature knows no perjury.
Order both cow-elephants, Lakshmi and Gauri, brought to the royal parade grounds immediately.'

The two mother elephants were brought to opposite sides of the vast arena, held by their mahouts fifty paces apart.
The young calf was placed in the exact center of the dusty field, untied and free.

Tenali commanded both merchants: 'Call your elephants, and let the mothers call their child!'

Madhav shouted commands, and his elephant Gauri flapped her ears indifferently, looking toward the river, chewing sugarcane.
Then Keshav spoke gentle, rhythmic words in the forest dialect.
His elephant Lakshmi lifted her trunk high into the air and let out a soft, deep, rumbling maternal trumpet of profound longing!

The moment the little calf heard Lakshmi’s rumble, its ears perked up!
The calf ignored Madhav’s elephant completely, let out a joyous squeal, and galloped as fast as its stubby legs could carry it across the sand!
It ran straight to Lakshmi, ducked beneath her belly, nuzzled against her front leg, and began nursing greedily!
Lakshmi wrapped her great trunk tenderly around the calf's back, caressing its ears with maternal adoration!

Tenali turned to the King and the assembly:
'Look, Maharaj! No calf ever nurses from a stranger, nor does a mother elephant caress another’s offspring with such tender devotion!
Nature has delivered the verdict: the calf belongs to Keshav!'

The assembly cheered the undeniable truth of nature.
Madhav was fined fifty gold coins for theft and perjury, Keshav was reunited with his elephants, and King Krishnadevaraya praised Tenali’s profound understanding of maternal instinct.
moral: Nature's maternal bonds cannot be deceived by forged sales deeds; the mother's heart identifies her true offspring.
